title: Stranded Faroese shawl
subtitle: A Faroese-construction DK shawl with a stranded colourwork yoke at the shoulder gussets.
excerpt: A Faroese-shaped DK shawl with stranded colourwork worked across the shoulder gusset sections and the uppermost rows of the centre back. Garter stitch fills the lower wings. Wingspan approximately 155 cm, total depth approximately 78 cm. About 300 g of main colour plus 120 g of contrast colour.
sourceNotes: The stranded Faroese shawl is a traditional form combining the shoulder gusset construction documented in Anny Evermann, Die Norwegischen Muster in der Strickerei (1902) with stranded colourwork. The specific colourwork motif here, a simple 8-stitch chevron, is a generic Shetland-tradition form documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Colour Patterns.

glossaryTerms.definition: A shawl construction from the Faroe Islands with five sections: a centre back panel, two wings, and two shoulder gussets. The gussets create a curved shoulder fit. In the stranded version, colourwork is worked at the gussets and upper centre back where the shawl sits across the shoulders.

In stranded colourwork worked flat, the colour carried consistently below the other. It sits slightly lower in the stitch and reads more prominently. Choose a dominant colour before the first colourwork row and maintain it throughout.

content.text: DK shawl with stranded colourwork across the gusset sections and upper centre back. Wingspan approximately 155 cm, depth approximately 78 cm.

The colourwork chevron pattern occupies the first 20 rows of the shawl, where the gusset shaping runs and the shawl sits over the shoulders. Below the gusset, the wings continue in plain garter stitch in the main colour. Set the
before row 1 and maintain it throughout the colourwork section. Budget about 300 g of main colour (MC) and 120 g of contrast (CC) in DK wool.

content.text: 22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. The colourwork section typically runs 1 to 2 stitches tighter per 10 cm than garter; the gusset section is short (approximately 7 to 10 RS rows) so the slight draw-in is minimal.
Cast on 81 stitches as for the plain Faroese shawl: 6 left wing, 15 left gusset, 39 centre back, 15 right gusset, 6 right wing. Place 4 section markers.

Work the Faroese shaping (gusset decreases, wing increases) as set, substituting a chevron colourwork pattern for plain garter in the gusset and centre-back sections only. Chevron motif (8 sts, RS row): *k4 MC, k4 CC; repeat from *. Alternate sections shift the CC block by 1 stitch each RS row for a diagonal chevron effect.
Once the gusset sections are complete (approximately 7 RS rows), break CC and continue in MC garter stitch. Work wing increases until wingspan reaches 155 cm.
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off in MC.

Colourwork floats too short in gusset sections: the float length must match the 15-stitch gusset width. Spread the stitches on the needle before working the float to prevent the gusset from pulling in.
Colour bleed between gusset and wing on WS rows: carry both yarns loosely across the section markers so the float ends do not pull the marker inward.
Wet-block as for the plain Faroese shawl. The colourwork section should be checked for dye bleed before blocking: test a small swatch of CC in cool water on a white cloth.
Hand wash gently in cool water to avoid agitating the colourwork floats. Lay flat to dry.
Extend the colourwork section to the first 40 rows instead of 20. This creates a deeper colourwork yoke reaching into the upper wing before switching to plain garter.
